{{Quote|Come on To'iir! We've got no time to hang around here! Roff will have hunters on us in no time!''"</br>"''Young one, we have no time to spare indeed. I waste not time. I plan. Witness.|Liadden and To'iir|<ref name="J10" />}}
'''To'iir''' was an elderly [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and the owner of the [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] ''[[Seventy-Seven Stars]]''. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], he mentored the young [[Human/Legends|Human]] girl [[Liadden]], one of his many partners. At some point, the pair had attracted the attention of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Roff]] and planned on departing their current [[Star system/Legends|star system]]. To'iir, using the the [[Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood/Legends|Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood]]-provided [[Free-Trader's Guide|Free Trader's Guide]], retrieved several worlds that lay within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and [[The Slice/Legends|The Slice]]. From the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] candidates [[Chad/Legends|Chad]], [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]], and [[Toola/Legends|Toola]], To'iir decided to travel to Gamorr, frustrating Liadden.

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], To'iir, Liadden, and the Twi'lek gunrunner [[Tru'eb Cholakk]], were guests of the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Rithgar]] at his [[Kothlis shadowport|shadowport]], located on the second [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the planet [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]]. While there, the Twi'leks communicated secretly with their [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]] to gather intelligence, which Liadden was able to pick up on. The guests' visit was eventually interrupted by an Imperial [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]], causing To'iir to make a hasty exit with Liadden.

==Biography==
===Into the galaxy===
[[File:Head-clan death.jpg|thumb|right|300px|To'iir hailed from the Outer Rim planet Ryloth (pictured).]]
To'iir was a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who left his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]],<ref name="J10" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], to become a [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] of the drug [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. He procured the [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] ''[[Seventy-Seven Stars]]'' and traveled [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], earning and losing many fortunes, trading, and going through many partners. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]<ref name="J10" /> between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="SOTES">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> he was elderly and had gained a new partner, the eighteen-[[Standard year/Legends|year]]-old [[Human/Legends|Human]] girl [[Liadden]]. He saw her as a niece and tried to pass down the lessons he had learned in his years of "riding [[Heat storm|heatstorms]]."<ref name="J10" />

===Finding refuge===
{{Quote|Well?''"<br/>"''Gamorr.''"<br/>"''Gamorr! Those barbarians? You're kidding! Tell me your kidding! They'll rip us to shreds!''"<br/>"''Hmm, probably not. We do alright. Gamorr is long enough away that Roff forget about us a little. Besides, they pay cash.|Liadden and To'iir, moments before the former storms away|<ref name="J10" />}}
[[File:Chad.jpg|thumb|left|300px|To'iir pulled up an entry on Chad (pictured) for Liadden to examine.]]
At some point, Liadden and To'iir had to escape from the Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Roff]]. While aboard the ''Seventy-Seven Stars'' in a [[Star system/Legends|star system]], Liadden urged To'iir to leave, as Roff would have hunters on them soon. Gazing calmly at the girl, To'iir agreed with her and made her watch as he pulled up the [[Free-Trader's Guide]], provided by the [[Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood/Legends|Lantillian Spacers Brotherhood]], on the ship's [[datacomp station]]. The Twi'lek typed in the restricted feature [[Trader's Gamble]], entered his password, and got accepted in. He then pared down 4112 entries into Outer Rim locations, those 682 locations into [[The Slice/Legends|The Slice]] locations and finally refined those locations into ones categorized with "[[Spaceport/Legends|Starports]] of Limited Service or less."<ref name="J10" />

Liadden, fuming and impatient, was not impressed and reiterated that they needed to leave. To'iir, amused and patient in contrast, asked her where they would go, then briskly tapped in some commands. As the Twi'lek reviewed his data, Liadden urged him to go to the first location on his list, the planet [[Altor 14]], only for To'iir to decline because of the native [[Species/Legends|species]] there. He then reflected that his partner should pick a place with little Imperial presence and reminded her of Roff. To'iir then pulled up an entry on the planet [[Chad/Legends|Chad]] for Liadden to examine.<ref name="J10" />

[[File:Gamorr SWJ10.jpg|thumb|right|350px|To'iir settled on hiding out on Gamorr (pictured).]]
To'iir's partner felt positive about Chad and exclaimed for them to go, just for the Twi'lek to disagree because the humidity and [[Temperature/Legends|heat]] would be bad for his joints. Liadden pushed back, but To'iir was firm on his judgement and told her they might visit the world someday. He then scanned the next entry, the planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]]. Liadden felt the world was dangerous and remarked she did not know the native [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] traded. To'iir replied that the species was simple and like everyone else, then contemplated hiding on the planet's "winterside," though ended up scrolling to the next entry, the planet [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]]. Liadden, a [[Insect/Legends|bug]] hater, did not feel like traveling to the world, and so did To'iir. Though the food there could be delicious, he viewed it as busy, advanced, and not safe if there was an Imperial presence.<ref name="J10" />

After they viewed the next entry, the planet [[Toola/Legends|Toola]], To'iir settled on Gamorr, much to Liadden's dismay. The Twi'lek reasoned that they would do alright there, and it was far enough away Roff might forget about them somewhat. He additionally rationalized it by stating the Gamorreans payed in [[Currency/Legends|cash]]. The old man turned back to the datacomp station and wondered where they would get [[Vibro-ax/Legends|vibro-axes]] or [[Shield (physical armor)/Legends|shields]], then pondered if the Gamorreans had ever thought of shields. Liadden, frustrated, stormed off to her bunk.<ref name="J10" />

===A visit and an exit===
{{Quote|Come, young one. Hasty exit. Imperial problems not good&hellip; not now.|To'iir to Liadden|<ref name="HE" />}}
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date">The [[Cynabar's InfoNet/Legends|Cynabar's InfoNet]] segment of {{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}} is dated to 38:4:31 [[Great ReSynchronization|G.R.S.]], which corresponds to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> To'iir and Liadden made the "[[Spirva Run]]" by hauling some loads of [[Gladiator walker|gladiator walkers]] to the [[Spirva sector/Legends|Spirva sector]], a then-rioting region kept under martial law. The pair was eventually caught however, and the pair's predicament was reported on in the [[Cynabar's InfoNet/Legends|Cynabar's InfoNet]] news service on the [[Great ReSynchronization|Grand ReSynchronization]] [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] 38:4:31. The report speculated that To'iir and Liadden were heading to<ref name="J14">{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Rithgar|Rithgar's]] [[Kothlis shadowport|shadowport]], located on the second [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of<ref name="SOTES" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &#x2014; Based on corresponding data for [[Kothlis system/Legends|Kothlis system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]].<ref name="J14" /> 

[[File:Hasty_Exit_illustration.jpg|thumb|left|300px|To'iir, Liadden, and Tru'eb Cholakk visited Rithgar's shadowport]]
To'iir and Liadden eventually made it to Kothlis's second moon, where they refueled their starship and acquired some spare sparts in exchange for their ship's stores. To'iir, Liadden, and the Twi'lek gunrunner [[Tru'eb Cholakk]] were then invited to Rithgar's shadowport quarters for drinks and discussion on their fellow smugglers. To'iir, who insisted on the visit, drank hot [[Caf/Legends|caffa]] while sitting on a divan with his apprentice. Rithgar discussed Roff's pursuit of them, and correlated Liadden's age with their circumstance. To'iir responded confidently, but the pirate was unable to tell whether the comment was about his starship or Liadden.<ref name="HE" />

Rithgar then changed the focus of their conversation to Cholakk, who had been sitting quietly. When the gunrunner mentioned his partner, [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]], doing work in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], To'iir asked if there were difficulties there. As Cholakk responded that she could handle it, his<ref name="HE" /> [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]]<ref name="EGAS" /> head-[[Limb/Legends|tails]] moved with his speech, perhaps to elaborate on his comment. The two continued their discussion about smugglers as their lekku added to their conversation. Liadden, watching the two Twi'leks, then realized they were trading notes with each other, and their visit was for intelligence gathering.<ref name="HE" />

Rithgar's computer sensors then began to sound in warning for an approaching Imperial [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]],<ref name="HE" /> the ''[[Executor/Legends|Executor]]''.<ref name="SOTES" /> To'iir and Liadden rose from their seat, the latter going to gather his belongings. Cholakk stopped before he exited the quarters and gave To'iir the parting phrase "ma-allesh," which the old man nodded back to. To'iir then grabbed his apprentice by the hand and dragged her out so they could make a hasty exit.<ref name="HE" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Great! Let's go!''"<br/>"''Hm. Humid and hot. Bad for my joints.''"<br/>"''Oh, come on! It's just a bolt hole! We won't be there long!''"<br/>"''We may be there sometime. Ship break down, fuel run low, local trouble maybe. Plan ahead. Maybe go to Chad, but I keep looking.|Liadden and To'iir|<ref name="J10" />}}
[[File:Liadden-Hasty_Exit.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Liadden (pictured) was like a niece to To'iir.]]
An aged man, To'iir suffered from a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] wound located on his hip and walked with a considerable limp.<ref name="J10" /> His<ref name="HE">{{WEGCite|story=Hasty Exit|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref> lekku<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> rested casually upon his shoulders,<ref name="HE" /> and came across as a patient and [[Parent/Legends|paternal]] figure due to the combination of his age, withering body, and experience. To'iir spoke in a broken manner and claimed that he would never retire.<ref name="J10" /> 

To'iir was the mentor of the young girl Liadden and passed down the lessons he had learned to her. He viewed her as a favored niece, and she thought of him as her favorite uncle. Both tried to keep the other out of trouble. The girl also aspired to one day travel [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] like he did and visit the areas her mentor stayed clear of.<ref name="J10" />

When Liadden suggested traveling to Altor 14, he declined as he did not like the Altorian inhabitants and thought his apprentice would start fights there. He found<ref name="J10" /> the [[Nuiwit]]<ref name="GG4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref> too passive and<ref name="J10" /> the [[Avogwi]]<ref name="GG4" /> too violent and unpredictable. To'iir assessed that the planet Chad's humidity and heat had negative effects on his joints. The Gamorreans,<ref name="J10" /> a species infamous for their slow minds,<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|I|318|Gamorrean}}</ref> were just like every other person to him, because they traded, had families, worked, [[Music/Legends|sang]], and fought.<ref name="J10" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|Lots of room to hide, and I think I still remember Gamorrean.|To'iir, on Gamorr|<ref name="J10" />}}
Like other Twi'leks, To'iir could use his lekku to secretly communicate with other members of his species.<ref name="J10" /> While at Rithgar's shadowport, he used this skill to gather communication from Tru'eb Cholakk.<ref name="HE" /> The trader was knowledgeable on several topics: [[Alien/Legends|alien]] species, cultures, [[Language/Legends|languages]], bureaucracy, business, planetary [[Star system/Legends|systems]], and value. He had streetwise and survival knowledge, also knowing how to hide himself. To'iir utilized several honed skills when dealing with other beings, such as conning, bargaining, [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] and persuasion. To'iir at one point knew the [[Gamorrese]] language.<ref name="J10" />

==Equipment==
The Twi'lek piloted the ''Seventy-Seven Stars'', a modified light-freighter that featured a datacomp station and one [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]]. To'iir [[Clothing/Legends|dressed]] himself in [[Robe/Legends|robes]] and used [[Polycarbonate/Legends|polycarbonate]]-lens reading [[spectacles]]. He armed himself with a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blaster]] and had a sling bag that carried various odds and ends of his, such as [[Engine/Legends|engine]] tape. Other possessions included ball-bearings of assorted sizes, five [[Meter/Legends|meters]] of rolled wire, a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]], and 500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. The Twi'lek ate snack [[Fungus/Legends|fungus]] and carried that and an eating [[Knife/Legends|knife]] with him.<ref name="J10" />

==Behind the scenes==
To'iir was introduced in "[[A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets]]," an article included in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 10|tenth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'', a magazine published by [[West End Games]] in [[May]] [[1996]] for use in ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="J10" /> The character was then first pictured in "[[Hasty Exit]]," a short story written by [[Peter M. Schweighofer]], illustrated by [[Storn Cook]], and included in the ''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]'' released in [[June]] 1996.<ref name="HE" />
